graph_metadata.title: Assembly Language — Detailed Machine-Readable Knowledge Graph
graph_metadata.subject: Assembly language, assemblers, instruction sets, object files, linking, and execution
graph_metadata.description: Architecture-aware knowledge graph representing assembly language syntax, assembler directives, registers, addressing modes, ISA families, toolchains, object formats, relocations, debugging, security, firmware workflows, and usage examples.
graph_metadata.scope_note: Assembly is not one universal language: syntax, mnemonics, register names, instruction encodings, directives, ABI rules, and object formats vary by ISA, assembler, platform, and toolchain.

source_basis.source_type: General technical knowledge and standard toolchain concepts
source_basis.freshness_note: Tool options, syntax, supported ISAs, ABI conventions, and security features vary by release and target. Validate examples on the intended platform.

serialization.id_policy: Stable lowercase snake_case entity IDs; sequential relationship IDs within this generated artifact.

entities.name: Assembly language
entities.description: A family of low-level programming languages whose symbolic instructions and directives correspond closely to a processor instruction set, object format, assembler, or toolchain.

entities.name: Assembly source file
entities.description: Text containing assembly instructions, labels, expressions, macros, and assembler directives.

entities.name: Assembler
entities.description: A program that parses assembly source, resolves symbols and expressions, encodes instructions, applies relocations, and emits object code or flat binary output.

entities.name: Machine code
entities.description: Processor-specific instruction encodings executed or interpreted by a processor or virtual machine.

entities.name: Object file
entities.description: Relocatable binary containing machine code, data, symbols, relocations, and optional debug or metadata sections.

entities.name: Executable image
entities.description: A linked program image loaded by an operating system, firmware, bootloader, or runtime.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Combines object files and libraries, resolves symbol references, applies relocations, and produces executable or library output.

entities.name: Program loader
entities.description: Operating-system, firmware, or runtime component that maps executable sections, applies dynamic relocations where needed, and transfers control to the entry point.

entities.name: Processor / CPU
entities.description: Hardware that fetches, decodes, and executes instructions according to an instruction-set architecture.

entities.name: Instruction-set architecture (ISA)
entities.description: The programmer-visible contract defining instructions, registers, addressing modes, memory model, privilege behavior, and encoding rules.

entities.name: Microarchitecture
entities.description: A particular implementation of an ISA, including pipelines, caches, execution units, and branch prediction.

entities.name: Application Binary Interface (ABI)
entities.description: Binary conventions for function calls, register use, stack layout, data layout, symbol naming, and interoperability.

entities.name: Calling convention
entities.description: Rules for passing arguments, returning values, preserving registers, and managing call frames.

entities.name: Object-file format
entities.description: Container specification for code/data sections, symbols, relocations, metadata, and debug information.

entities.name: Executable and Linkable Format (ELF)
entities.description: Object and executable format common on Linux and many Unix-like systems.

entities.name: Common Object File Format (COFF)
entities.description: Object format family used by various toolchains and platforms.

entities.name: PE/COFF
entities.description: Executable and object format used by Windows toolchains.

entities.name: Mach-O
entities.description: Object and executable format used by Apple platforms.

entities.name: Relocation
entities.description: A record describing how a symbol-dependent address or value must be adjusted by the assembler, linker, or loader.

entities.name: Symbol
entities.description: Named addressable entity such as a function, object, section, label, or externally resolved reference.

entities.name: Symbol table
entities.description: Object-file data that records symbol names, bindings, types, visibility, and associated locations.

entities.name: Section
entities.description: Named object-file region such as code, initialized data, uninitialized data, read-only constants, or metadata.

entities.name: Debug information
entities.description: Metadata mapping machine instructions and data to source locations, types, and symbols.

entities.name: Disassembler
entities.description: Tool that decodes machine-code bytes into assembly-like instruction text.

entities.name: Compiler
entities.description: Program that translates a higher-level language into a lower-level representation, assembly, or object code.

entities.name: Integrated assembler
entities.description: Assembler implementation embedded in a compiler toolchain, such as LLVM's integrated assembler.

entities.name: Macro assembler
entities.description: Assembler supporting textual or parameterized macros that expand into source constructs.

entities.name: Linker script
entities.description: Configuration describing memory regions, section placement, symbols, and layout for supported linkers.

entities.name: Startup code
entities.description: Entry-point and initialization code that prepares runtime state before invoking application code.

entities.name: Runtime library
entities.description: Library routines used by generated programs for initialization, arithmetic helpers, I/O, exceptions, or language runtime support.

entities.name: Firmware
entities.description: Software built to run on a device or bare-metal target, often with a custom memory map and startup sequence.

entities.name: Bare-metal environment
entities.description: Execution without a general-purpose operating system, requiring explicit startup, memory, and hardware setup.

entities.name: Operating system
entities.description: System software that loads processes, provides system calls, manages memory, and schedules execution.

entities.name: Source-level debugger
entities.description: Debugger that uses symbols and debug metadata to correlate machine execution with source or assembly.

entities.name: Profiler
entities.description: Tool that measures or samples program execution to identify performance costs.

entities.name: Assembler listing
entities.description: Human-readable output correlating source lines, addresses, encodings, and symbols.

entities.name: Flat binary image
entities.description: Raw bytes without the richer section/symbol metadata of a relocatable object file.

entities.name: Disassembly listing
entities.description: Textual rendering of machine-code instructions and optionally addresses, bytes, and symbol annotations.

entities.name: Instruction mnemonic
entities.description: Textual name for an instruction or pseudo-operation, such as MOV, ADD, JMP, LDR, or ADDQ.

entities.name: Assembly instruction
entities.description: An operation written using a mnemonic and zero or more operands, encoded according to the target ISA.

entities.name: Instruction operand
entities.description: A register, immediate constant, memory expression, label, symbol, or architecture-specific operand form.

entities.name: Register
entities.description: A named processor storage location used by instructions.

entities.name: General-purpose register
entities.description: Register commonly used for integer values, pointers, addresses, and arithmetic.

entities.name: Stack pointer
entities.description: Register conventionally tracking the current stack location.

entities.name: Frame/base pointer
entities.description: Register sometimes used to anchor a function's stack frame.

entities.name: Instruction pointer / program counter
entities.description: Register or architectural state identifying the current or next instruction address.

entities.name: Flags/status register
entities.description: Architectural state recording conditions or status produced by operations.

entities.name: Vector/SIMD register
entities.description: Register holding packed data for vector or single-instruction-multiple-data operations.

entities.name: Immediate operand
entities.description: Literal value encoded directly in an instruction where the ISA permits it.

entities.name: Memory operand
entities.description: Operand denoting a memory location, often expressed using a base register, index, scale, and displacement.

entities.name: Label
entities.description: Named location in assembly source used as a branch target or address reference.

entities.name: Local label
entities.description: Assembler-specific label scoped or numbered for local control flow.

entities.name: Global symbol
entities.description: Symbol exposed for reference from other object files or link units.

entities.name: External symbol
entities.description: Symbol reference resolved by the linker or another object/module.

entities.name: Assembler directive
entities.description: Non-CPU instruction that controls assembly, sections, symbols, alignment, data emission, or assembler behavior.

entities.name: Assembly comment
entities.description: Text ignored by the assembler according to the syntax and comment markers of the selected assembler.

entities.name: Assembly expression
entities.description: Constant or symbol expression evaluated by the assembler or linker where supported.

entities.name: Addressing mode
entities.description: Rule describing how an instruction identifies its operands or memory locations.

entities.name: Register addressing
entities.description: Operand is a register.

entities.name: Immediate addressing
entities.description: Operand is an immediate literal.

entities.name: Base-plus-displacement addressing
entities.description: Memory address is derived from a base register and displacement.

entities.name: Indexed addressing
entities.description: Memory address is derived from a base/index register combination, potentially with scale.

entities.name: PC-relative addressing
entities.description: Address or branch displacement is relative to the instruction pointer/program counter.

entities.name: Indirect addressing
entities.description: Operand location or branch target is obtained through a register or memory reference.

entities.name: Data width
entities.description: Width of an operand or data object, commonly measured in bits or bytes.

entities.name: Endianness
entities.description: Ordering of bytes in multi-byte values in memory or encoded data.

entities.name: Alignment
entities.description: Requirement or performance preference for addresses to be multiples of a given boundary.

entities.name: Instruction encoding
entities.description: Bit-level layout used to represent an instruction and its operands.

entities.name: Opcode
entities.description: Encoding field or bit pattern identifying an operation.

entities.name: Condition code
entities.description: Predicate used by conditional branches or predicated instructions.

entities.name: Branch instruction
entities.description: Instruction that changes the next instruction address, conditionally or unconditionally.

entities.name: Conditional branch
entities.description: Branch taken only when a condition is satisfied.

entities.name: Unconditional branch
entities.description: Branch that always transfers control to its target.

entities.name: Call instruction
entities.description: Transfers control to a subroutine and establishes return behavior according to the ISA/ABI.

entities.name: Return instruction
entities.description: Transfers control back to the caller according to the ISA/ABI.

entities.name: Stack frame
entities.description: Per-call storage region used for saved state, local variables, spills, and other ABI-defined data.

entities.name: Function prologue
entities.description: Initial function instructions that establish a stack frame or save required state.

entities.name: Function epilogue
entities.description: Final function instructions that restore state and return.

entities.name: Procedure / function
entities.description: A callable code region with entry, body, and return behavior.

entities.name: Inline assembly
entities.description: Assembly embedded inside a higher-level language, with compiler-specific constraints and clobber declarations.

entities.name: Volatile memory access
entities.description: Access whose observability constraints are defined by the language/compiler and target environment; not a general substitute for synchronization.

entities.name: Atomic operation
entities.description: Operation with atomicity and possibly ordering semantics defined by ISA, ABI, or language runtime.

entities.name: Memory barrier / fence
entities.description: Instruction or construct constraining the ordering or visibility of memory operations.

entities.name: Interrupt handler
entities.description: Routine entered due to an interrupt or exception under platform-specific rules.

entities.name: Trap / exception instruction
entities.description: Instruction or event that transfers control to an exception, fault, or trap handler.

entities.name: Code section directive
entities.description: Selects or declares a section intended for executable code.

entities.name: Initialized data section directive
entities.description: Selects or declares a section for initialized data.

entities.name: Zero-initialized data section directive
entities.description: Selects or declares a section for uninitialized or zero-initialized storage.

entities.name: Read-only data section directive
entities.description: Selects or declares a section for constants.

entities.name: Global symbol directive
entities.description: Makes a symbol externally visible according to the assembler/object format.

entities.name: External symbol directive
entities.description: Declares a symbol expected to be defined elsewhere.

entities.name: Alignment directive
entities.description: Aligns the location counter or data/code placement according to assembler-specific semantics.

entities.name: Byte data directive
entities.description: Emits byte-sized data values.

entities.name: Word data directive
entities.description: Emits data values of an assembler-defined word width.

properties.note: The meaning of 'word' varies by assembler and target.

entities.name: Long data directive
entities.description: Emits a target-defined long-width data value in GNU assembler syntax.

entities.name: Quad data directive
entities.description: Emits a 64-bit data value in GNU assembler syntax on common targets.

entities.name: String data directive
entities.description: Emits string bytes, with null termination behavior depending on directive.

entities.name: Symbol constant directive
entities.description: Defines a symbol as an expression value.

entities.name: Symbol type directive
entities.description: Provides symbol-type metadata in supported object formats.

entities.name: Symbol size directive
entities.description: Associates a size expression with a symbol in supported formats.

entities.name: Call-frame information directives
entities.description: Emit unwind/debug metadata describing stack frames.

entities.name: Include binary file directive
entities.description: Copies bytes from a file into the output.

entities.name: Include source directive
entities.description: Includes another assembler source file.

entities.name: Macro definition directive
entities.description: Defines an assembler macro using syntax specific to the assembler.

entities.name: Conditional assembly directive
entities.description: Includes or excludes source blocks according to assembly-time conditions.

entities.name: Architecture selection directive
entities.description: Selects an ISA extension, architecture, or instruction mode where supported.

entities.name: Syntax selection directive
entities.description: Selects a syntax dialect for supported target assemblers.

entities.name: Section selection directive
entities.description: Selects or creates an output section.

entities.name: Common symbol directive
entities.description: Requests storage for a common symbol according to assembler/linker conventions.

entities.name: File metadata directive
entities.description: Records source-file or compilation metadata.

entities.name: Origin/location directive
entities.description: Changes or specifies an output location/origin where supported; behavior varies by assembler and output mode.

entities.name: Repeated data directive
entities.description: Emits repeated data or reserves repeated space in assemblers that support it.

entities.name: End directive
entities.description: Assembler-specific marker for end of source or module.

entities.name: x86 ISA
entities.description: CISC instruction set used by IA-32 processors.

entities.name: x86-64 ISA
entities.description: 64-bit extension of x86 with additional registers and addressing capabilities.

entities.name: Arm 32-bit ISA
entities.description: 32-bit Arm instruction-set family with ARM and Thumb encodings depending on target.

entities.name: AArch64 ISA
entities.description: 64-bit Arm instruction set.

entities.name: RISC-V ISA
entities.description: Open ISA family with base instruction sets and optional extensions.

entities.name: Power ISA
entities.description: Instruction set used by PowerPC/Power systems.

entities.name: AVR ISA
entities.description: Instruction set for AVR microcontrollers.

entities.name: MIPS ISA
entities.description: RISC instruction-set family.

entities.name: IBM z/Architecture ISA
entities.description: Instruction set for IBM mainframe systems.

entities.name: NVIDIA PTX ISA
entities.description: Virtual instruction set for NVIDIA GPU programming toolchains.

entities.name: WebAssembly instruction set
entities.description: Portable stack-machine instruction set commonly produced by compilers rather than conventional native assemblers.

entities.name: eBPF instruction set
entities.description: Verified bytecode instruction set used in Linux kernel and related environments.

entities.name: MOS 6502 ISA
entities.description: 8-bit instruction set used in classic and embedded systems.

entities.name: Zilog Z80 ISA
entities.description: 8-bit instruction set used in embedded and legacy systems.

entities.name: Motorola 68000 ISA
entities.description: Instruction set for the 68000 processor family.

entities.name: GNU assembler (GNU as)
entities.description: Assembler distributed with GNU Binutils, commonly invoked as as and used in GCC toolchains.

entities.name: NASM
entities.description: Netwide Assembler, commonly used for x86 and x86-64 with Intel-like syntax.

entities.name: Yasm
entities.description: Assembler designed for x86 and x86-64, supporting NASM-like syntax and multiple output formats.

entities.name: Microsoft Macro Assembler (MASM)
entities.description: Microsoft assembler commonly used for x86/x64 Windows development.

entities.name: Flat Assembler (FASM)
entities.description: Assembler known for direct binary and executable output workflows.

entities.name: LLVM MC / integrated assembler
entities.description: LLVM machine-code framework and integrated assembler used by Clang and other LLVM tools.

entities.name: Arm assembler toolchain
entities.description: Arm assembler implementations and syntax used by Arm development toolchains; exact syntax varies by tool/version.

entities.name: RISC-V GNU toolchain
entities.description: Cross-toolchain including assembler, linker, compiler, and binary utilities for RISC-V.

entities.name: GNU Binutils
entities.description: Tool suite containing GNU assembler, linker, and binary inspection utilities.

entities.name: objdump
entities.description: Displays object-file information and disassembles machine code.

entities.name: readelf
entities.description: Displays ELF file headers, sections, symbols, and relocation information.

entities.name: nm
entities.description: Lists symbols from object files and executables.

entities.name: objcopy
entities.description: Copies and transforms object files, including conversion to raw binary in supported workflows.

entities.name: GNU Debugger (GDB)
entities.description: Debugger that can inspect registers, memory, symbols, and assembly instructions.

entities.name: Linux perf
entities.description: Linux performance analysis tool that can sample execution and annotate machine instructions.

entities.name: Compiler Explorer
entities.description: Online tool for exploring compiler-generated assembly; availability and supported compilers vary.

entities.name: GNU Make
entities.description: Build automation tool commonly used to invoke assemblers and linkers.

entities.name: CMake
entities.description: Build-system generator that can configure assembly and mixed-language projects.

entities.name: QEMU
entities.description: Machine emulator and virtualizer useful for running code built for supported target architectures.

entities.name: GDB Remote Serial Protocol
entities.description: Protocol used by GDB to debug remote targets, including embedded hardware.

entities.name: DWARF
entities.description: Debugging information format used by many ELF toolchains.

entities.name: Unwind metadata
entities.description: Metadata enabling stack unwinding, exceptions, profilers, or debuggers depending on platform.

entities.name: Binary security mitigations
entities.description: Compiler/assembler/linker/platform mechanisms such as NX, PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, and control-flow protection.

entities.name: Position-independent executable (PIE)
entities.description: Executable built to support relocation to varying virtual addresses where platform/toolchain support exists.

entities.name: Position-independent code (PIC)
entities.description: Code generated to execute correctly when loaded at varying addresses, often used in shared libraries.

entities.name: Stack canary
entities.description: Runtime check intended to detect certain stack-buffer overwrite patterns.

entities.name: NX / execute-disable protection
entities.description: Hardware/OS mechanism marking memory regions non-executable.

entities.name: RELRO
entities.description: ELF hardening technique that makes selected relocation-related data read-only after relocation.

entities.name: Control-flow integrity
entities.description: Mechanisms that constrain indirect control transfers to reduce exploitation opportunities.

entities.name: Call-frame information emission
entities.description: Assembler directives describing frame layout and unwind rules.

entities.name: Inline assembly constraints
entities.description: Compiler annotations specifying operand forms, outputs, inputs, and clobbered state for embedded assembly.

entities.name: Assembly phase
entities.description: Parses assembly source, resolves local expressions/symbols, encodes instructions, and emits object or binary output.

entities.name: Compilation phase
entities.description: Translates a higher-level language into assembly or object code.

entities.name: Link phase
entities.description: Resolves cross-object symbols, selects libraries, lays out sections, and applies relocations.

entities.name: Load phase
entities.description: Maps an executable into memory and transfers control to its entry point.

entities.name: Cross-assembly
entities.description: Assembly performed for a target ISA different from the host CPU or platform.

entities.name: Embedded / bare-metal build
entities.description: Build process for firmware with target-specific startup code, linker script, memory layout, and runtime assumptions.

entities.name: Mixed-language build
entities.description: Build combining assembly and higher-level language objects with compatible ABI and symbol conventions.

entities.name: Function call sequence
entities.description: Coordinated steps involving argument passing, return address, stack/frame handling, register preservation, and return.

entities.name: Interrupt vector table
entities.description: Target-specific table mapping interrupt or exception numbers to handler addresses.

entities.name: Memory map
entities.description: Definition of address ranges for flash, RAM, peripherals, and reserved regions.

entities.name: Entry-point symbol
entities.description: Symbol chosen as program entry by linker configuration, OS format, or firmware startup convention.

entities.name: Inspect endianness-sensitive data
entities.description: Example concept for reasoning about how multi-byte values are stored and loaded.

entities.name: Minimal x86-64 Linux assembly example
entities.description: Illustrative GNU as Intel-syntax source using Linux system-call conventions; target-specific and not a portable ABI.

properties.source:
.intel_syntax noprefix
.global _start
.section .text
_start:
  mov eax, 60
  xor edi, edi
  syscall
properties.build: as --64 -o exit.o exit.s && ld -o exit exit.o
properties.note: Exits with status 0; it does not print text.

entities.name: NASM flat-binary skeleton
entities.description: Illustrative NASM syntax skeleton for a flat binary, requiring a specific load address and execution environment.

properties.note: Not a complete boot sector; boot protocol, signature, memory setup, and hardware assumptions are omitted.

entities.name: Define code and data sections
entities.description: Illustrates using section and data directives in GNU as.

entities.name: Function symbol and metadata
entities.description: Illustrates function labels, global visibility, and ELF symbol size metadata.

properties.note: Illustrative GNU as AT&T syntax; argument and return conventions follow the stated ABI.

entities.name: Inline assembly in C
entities.description: Illustrates a compiler extended-assembly statement with explicit output, input, and clobber constraints.

properties.note: Illustrative constraint syntax only; an empty asm with a memory clobber is a compiler barrier in GCC/Clang contexts, not a hardware fence.

entities.name: Disassemble an ELF executable
entities.description: Inspect instructions and symbol labels with objdump.

entities.name: Inspect object symbols
entities.description: List symbols in an object file.

entities.name: Inspect ELF sections
entities.description: Read ELF headers and section metadata.

entities.name: Convert object to raw binary
entities.description: Convert supported object output to a flat binary, typically for firmware or ROM images.

properties.note: Output omits object metadata and follows objcopy/target semantics.

entities.name: Assemble NASM to ELF64 object
entities.description: Assemble x86-64 source into an ELF relocatable object.

properties.command: nasm -f elf64 source.asm -o source.o && ld -o program source.o
properties.note: A real program needs a valid entry point and suitable runtime/syscall or library integration.

entities.name: Assemble with GNU as
entities.description: Assemble x86-64 source into an ELF object.

properties.note: Target options and syntax vary by architecture.

entities.name: Generate assembly from C
entities.description: Use GCC to emit assembly for inspection.

properties.note: Compiler-generated assembly is target-, compiler-version-, and flag-dependent.

entities.name: Link assembly with C
entities.description: Compile C and assemble a compatible assembly module, then link the objects.

properties.note: Symbols, calling convention, stack alignment, object format, and ABI must agree.

entities.name: Cross-assemble for AArch64
entities.description: Use a target-prefixed assembler and linker for an AArch64 target.

properties.note: The target toolchain and syntax must match the intended AArch64 environment.

entities.name: Debug assembly with GDB
entities.description: Start a debugger and inspect instructions and registers.

entities.name: Profile machine instructions
entities.description: Use Linux perf to sample and annotate a program.

properties.note: Permissions, kernel configuration, and hardware support may affect availability.

entities.name: Use a linker script
entities.description: Pass a custom linker script to a linker for embedded memory layout.

properties.note: Memory regions and entry point must match the actual device and startup implementation.
